pollster: Oklahoma Center for Education Policy (University of Oklahoma)
question: Should Oklahoma teacher salaries be increased, kept the same, or decreased
note: sup = greatly increase (34) + increase (37); opp = decrease (4) + greatly decrease (2); 22% stay the same. Adults, RDD cell sample.

question: Support raising pay for West Virginia educators and school service personnel
note: Online survey of WV voters Feb 23-25, 2026; 60 strongly + 30 somewhat support; opposition not reported. Sponsor not named; question battery reads like an advocacy poll, so tiered 3.

question: Make permanent the state support raising Missouri's minimum teacher starting salary from $25,000 to $38,000
note: Likely voters, Aug 8-16, 2022; opposition not reported in article.

pollster: University of New Hampshire Survey Center (Granite State Poll)
question: Support raising local teacher pay even if it increases the school district budget
note: Oct 13-17, 2022; opposition not reported in article.

pollster: PDK Poll (Phi Delta Kappa / Langer Research)
question: Support raising teacher salaries in your community even if it means higher property taxes
note: Adults; 66% said teachers are underpaid. Opposition not given in article; n approx 1,000.

question: Approve or disapprove of private school vouchers (state money for private school tuition) in Pennsylvania
note: Reversed: sup = % disapproving of vouchers (36 strongly + 18 somewhat); opp = % approving (22+14). 10% unsure. Likely voters, Sept 12-18, 2024.

pollster: Hobby School of Public Affairs (Univ. of Houston) & Texas Southern University / YouGov (Texas Trends)
question: Support or oppose school vouchers for all Texas parents
note: Reversed: sup = % opposing vouchers for all parents; opp = % supporting. Remainder neutral/unsure. Adults, Oct 6-18, 2023. Other versions: low-income-only vouchers 49 support/27 oppose; SB1 ESAs 41/24.

question: Support or oppose Gov. Lee's universal school voucher plan in Tennessee
note: Reversed: sup = % opposing vouchers (46); opp = % supporting (45); 9% neither. Spring 2024 Vanderbilt Poll of registered voters; exact dates/n not in article (fielded approx. Apr-May 2024).

pollster: Oklahoma Center for Education Policy (University of Oklahoma)
question: Support or oppose giving families a tax refund for private school tuition (Oklahoma's private school tax credit)
note: Reversed: sup = % opposing the private-school tax credit (11 oppose + 33 strongly oppose); opp = % supporting (30+17). 8% neither. Tax-credit voucher equivalent, not a classic voucher.

question: Prefer electing the president by national popular vote rather than the Electoral College
note: Adults, Aug 26-Sep 2, 2024 (American Trends Panel). Figures read via nationalpopularvote.com/node/448 summary of the Pew release.

question: Amend the Constitution so the president is elected by national popular vote instead of the Electoral College
note: Reported Sept 2024; opposition share not given in the article.

question: Keep the Electoral College or switch to electing the candidate who wins the national popular vote
note: Registered voters; rolling tracking estimate as of Nov 5, 2026 (trend since July 2023); 7% unsure. Civiqs is a Democratic-aligned firm. Civiqs site shows a state map but state values could not be extracted (JS-rendered; direct download blocked).

question: Favor or oppose automatically registering all eligible citizens to vote
note: Adults, Aug 4-10, 2025 (ATP); asked of Form 1 half-sample (n=1,770 of 3,554). opp = 21 somewhat + 19 strongly oppose. Dems 77% favor, Reps 42%.

pollster: AP-NORC Center for Public Affairs Research
question: Favor or oppose automatic voter registration
note: Published Apr 2, 2021; fieldwork dates/n not given in article (approx. March 2021). Opposition not reported.

question: Support having independent citizen commissions draw electoral districts
note: Registered voters, Aug 26-Sep 3, 2025; national n=2,016 plus state samples CA 484, FL 499, IL 490, NY 482, TX 400. Hybrid opt-in panel/text-to-web. Advocacy sponsor (Common Cause). Opposition not reported. State figures from indypolitics.org write-up (https://indypolitics.org/poll-finds-broad-opposition-to-mid-decade-redistricting/). Same poll: 60% oppose letting parties redraw districts mid-decade.

question: Prefer redistricting done by a nonpartisan commission rather than by the party in power
note: Aug 13-Sep 1, 2025; n not given in the IVN write-up. 71% of Republicans in GOP-run states and 88% of Democrats in Dem-run states preferred a commission. Opposition not reported.

question: Approve of the 2025 mid-decade redraw of Texas congressional districts
note: Reversed proxy: sup = % disapproving of the partisan mid-decade redraw (41), opp = % approving (34). Registered voters, Aug 22-Sep 1, 2025. Same poll asked about moving redistricting to an independent commission but the topline was not in the article or chart text.

question: Agree that gerrymandering should be illegal in Indiana
note: Registered voters, online, Aug 18-21, 2025. Change Research is a Democratic-aligned firm. Same poll: 52% opposed the 2025 mid-decade redraw (34% support).

question: Partisan gerrymandering should be illegal
note: Early August 2025, as reported by Sinclair/ABC6; exact dates, n and opposition not given. 76% call it a major problem.

question: Support Puerto Rico becoming a state if its residents voted for it
note: Puerto Rico half of the measure only; adults, Oct 28, 2024; 25% unsure. Conditional on PR residents voting for statehood.

question: Support or oppose making Washington, DC a state
note: DC half of the measure; adult citizens, Apr 25-27, 2021; 27% unsure. Same poll: Puerto Rico statehood 43% support / 31% oppose.

question: Minnesota Legislature needs to do more to stop fraud in state programs
note: Proxy for support for stronger anti-fraud oversight, not a question on audits/inspector general specifically. Published June 19, 2026; dates/n not in article. 73% said Gov. Walz needs to do more; 81% call fraud the biggest or a major problem.

question: Preventing fraud in public benefit programs should come first even if stricter rules limit access
note: Registered voters, Jan 13-19, 2026. opp = % prioritizing access even if some fraud continues. Weak proxy for gov:fraud; Democratic-aligned firm.

question: Minnesota Legislature needs to do more to stop fraud in state programs (vs. has done enough)
note: Proxy for support for stronger anti-fraud oversight, not a question on audits/inspector general specifically. Registered voters; published Dec 13, 2025. opp = % saying Legislature has done enough. Same poll: 69% say Gov. Walz needs to do more, 14% done enough.

question: Favor or oppose automatic voter registration in Pennsylvania
note: Registered voters; reported in the Delaware County Daily Times Apr 5, 2024 (field dates/n not given; F&M spring 2024 poll, approx. March 2024). PA adopted AVR at PennDOT by executive action in Sept 2023.

pollster: UNH Survey Center (Pine Tree State Poll)
question: Support or oppose Maine joining the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact
note: Poll dated Aug 22, 2024 (Maine enacted the compact in April 2024); n not given in article; remainder neutral/unsure. 1st District 43% support.
